request.spec: Return 'initials' as the upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot, e.g. 'J.S.'.
request.prompt:
Implement the following change to the application so that it fully satisfies
the specification and all existing and new tests pass. Run the test suite and
make it green before finishing.

Return 'initials' as the upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot, e.g. 'J.S.'.

agent.result_text:
There's only one test class, and the full suite is green (`BUILD SUCCESS`, 1 test passed, 0 failures/errors).

## Summary

I implemented the `initials` field on the owner API so that a GET on `/api/owners/{id}` returns the upper-cased first letters of `firstName` and `lastName`, dot-separated with a trailing dot (e.g. `J.S.`).

Two changes, following the existing `displayName` pattern already in the codebase:

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `initials` property to the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` gains the field.

2. **`src/main/java/.../mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** — added a `@Mapping(target = "initials", ...)` with a `@Named("formatInitials")` method that computes `initial(firstName) + initial(lastName)`, where each initial is the upper-cased first character followed by a dot (gracefully handling null/empty names).

The acceptance test `AcceptanceTest.coreComputesInitials` (which posts `john`/`smith` and expects `$.initials` = `J.S.`) passes, and the full suite builds green.

code_review.final_verdict:
VERDICT: LGTM

The new `formatInitials` method sits exactly where its sibling `formatDisplayName` already lives, and mirrors the established pattern in this interface precisely: a `@Named` default method with a null guard, matching Javadoc (including the identical `@Named`-rationale paragraph), referenced via `qualifiedByName` from the `toOwnerDto` mapping. The private `initial` helper is well-placed — it factors out the shared first-letter logic so firstName/lastName aren't handled twice, and keeps the formatting concern local to the mapper rather than leaking into the model or a utility catch-all. The OpenAPI addition parallels the adjacent `displayName` field (title/description/example/`readOnly`). Nothing is duplicated and no unit is becoming a grab-bag; a maintainer of this codebase would find it natural.
